parsed.explanation: The combined regime is broadly protective: gender identity is covered by hate-crime (2018) and hate-speech (2019) law with a functioning national crime dataset, institutions work, and the country ranks at the top of third-party LGBT travel indices. No border, document, custody, or police-targeting exposure against trans visitors is documented. The worst documented traveller-facing item is a national swimming-pool chain's changing-room restriction reaching ordinary public facilities — a real but narrow, contested, private-operator exposure, tier-2/3 at most. Minor-related care restrictions (under-16 blocker/hormone stop at one institution, 2022 cautious guidance) affect a travelling family only if care was sought; prescriptions have risen slightly, and it is guidance, not a statutory ban. Organised political opposition and harassment of advocates sits largely in the resident sphere. No criminalisation; severity if outed is low.

entry_documents.protection: No LGBTQ entry rules sourced; nothing indicates marker scrutiny or refusal at entry for solo adults or families.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry is a national competence; no adverse practice recorded at any border stage.

investigation_detention_custody.protection: Working courts and hate-crime statute imply recourse; no custody-placement risk recorded.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Rule of law mediates: strong institutions, no documented hostile enforcement.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National swimming-pool chain since Oct 2025 bars trans customers from choosing changing rooms — reaches ordinary public facilities, legally contested; scope beyond the chain unknown.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Applies to visitors equally; a minor faces the same restriction as an adult.

care_services.exposure: One major institution stopped blockers/hormones for under-16s (2021); 2022 authority guidance restricts blockers to exceptional cases — applies if a travelling minor needs care. Visitor care access itself not documented.
care_services.protection: Guidance not statutory ban; 2026 data show prescriptions rising; depathologisation 2017.
care_services.interaction: A guardian travelling with a minor on medication may face refills outside trials being refused.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Organised opposition (far-right/Christian-democrat parties, women's umbrella platform framing trans reform as threat); scholarly record of harassment, threats and vilification of advocates.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Hate-speech law exists but contested: imam not prosecuted, preacher acquitted on religious-speech grounds.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Mostly resident-sphere; frames climate, not visitor targeting.

minors_guardians.exposure: For a travelling 16–17-year-old, domestic LGR requires guardian consent; under-16 clinical access limited to trials; surgery age floors are resident-facing.
minors_guardians.protection: Care restrictions are guidance-based, not criminalising; nothing documented reaching visiting families at entry or in daily life.
minors_guardians.interaction: These are resident-pathway rules; visitor exposure is indirect and undocumented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: National hate-crime dataset records offences with police-identified LGBTQI motives; unreported hostility unmeasured. No visitor-specific violence documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Gender identity in hate-crime law since 2018, hate speech since 2019; police recording practice exists and works.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse is documented and operative, though prosecution of hate speech is uneven.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Changing-room restriction scope beyond one chain unknown; conversion-practices bill status unresolved; hate-speech enforcement uneven (religious-speech acquittals).
remedies_unknowns.protection: Counselling centres in three cities; compensation precedent for past wrongs shows institutional accountability.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Open questions are lighter than exposures under the rubric.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier: statutory hate-crime protection, functioning oversight, occasional facility friction (shelter hesitation vs. pool chain). Anonymised jurisdiction shows no documented officer stops, so slightly better on street-police axis.

Below 0.95-C: that anchor shows strong enforced health protections nationwide; here clinical access has narrowed for minors and a documented facility restriction exists with contested remedies, subtracting materially.

Well above: 0.55-C features ward assignment by documents causing routine denial of care. Here care restriction is institution/guidance-scoped, hate-crime recourse works, and no universal document or ward exposure is documented.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines strong protective law (gender identity in hate-crime and hate-speech statutes since 2018/2019, a working national recording dataset, functioning courts, top-tier third-party travel standing) with two documented narrow exposures: a single national pool chain's changing-room rule reaching ordinary public facilities, and minor-scoped clinical restrictions on blockers/hormones that could affect a travelling family seeking refills. Neither is criminalising, universal-exposure, or state-enforced against visitors; both are contested. Organised political opposition and vilification of advocates are resident-sphere signals that colour but do not target the traveller. Severity if outed is low — humiliation and service friction, not custody — with real recourse. Net: high safety, a step below the 0.95 tier because of the documented facility restriction and narrowed minor care.
